item.title: Trump threatens Iran with "decapitation" as Houthis claim strike on Saudi airport
item.description: Trump threatened Tehran with "decapitation" Monday, before Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis claimed to have struck a Saudi airport.

item.title: What to watch for in SpaceX's first public earnings report today
item.description: SpaceX will release its first earnings report as a public company on Tuesday in a key test for the company's stuttering stock price.

item.title: SpaceX rocket is on a 5,400-mph collision course with the moon
item.description: The impact will not be visible to the naked eye, but photos are expected to come from a lunar satellite at a later time.

item.title: Full interview: Haley Stevens on race against Abdul El-Sayed, views on Israel and Trump
item.description: Michigan Rep. Haley Stevens, a moderate, is facing off against progressive Abdul El-Sayed in the Democratic Senate primary that is highlighting splits among some Democrats over their priorities. CBS News senior White House and political correspondent Ed O'Keefe spoke to Stevens about her opponent, her views on President Trump's administration, and the questions about American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) donations for her campaign.

item.title: Can creditors freeze your savings account over an unpaid debt?
item.description: Creditors have many tools to use if you're delinquent on debt payments, but are savings account levies one of them?

item.title: Full Interview: Abdul El-Sayed makes progressive case as Democrats weigh race against Haley Stevens
item.description: Progressive Abdul El-Sayed, a doctor by trade, is facing off against Moderate Rep. Haley Stevens in the Michigan Senate primary, which reflects the split among some Democrats over their voting priorities. CBS News senior White House and political correspondent Ed O'Keefe spoke to El-Sayed about his Senate bid, his view on the Democratic Socialists of America, and how he would work alongside established Democrats if he makes it to Capitol Hill.

item.title: Serviceman kills 3 civilians, 1 soldier in Russian-held Crimea
item.description: A serviceman in Russian-held Crimea opened fire on fellow soldiers and civilians, killing four people and wounding four, officials said.

item.title: Nearly 25% of Americans say CEOs are too greedy, survey shows
item.description: A new survey examined Americans' attitudes and perceptions toward CEOs and extreme wealth concentration. CBS News contributor Javier E. David responds.

item.title: Washington wildfires "likely the worst natural disaster in Spokane's history," governor says
item.description: Officials arrested a man on suspicion of arson as the Spokane, Washington, area battles multiple fires. Fire crews are working around the clock to contain the massive blazes. CBS News' Kris Van Cleave reports.

item.title: What to expect from July's jobs report
item.description: CBS News business analyst Jill Schlesinger joins CBS News 24/7 to discuss the upcoming jobs report by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics and the state of the economy. (Sponsored by AT&T Business)

item.title: SpaceX crew prepares for 6-month mission; NASA renders show lumpy Earth without oceans
item.description: SpaceX's next crew shared their excitement about an upcoming spaceflight. Plus, NASA's newest rendering of Earth shows a lumpy, not-quite-spherical planet. CBS News space consultant Bill Harwood shares his reaction.

item.title: First deaths linked to cyclospora parasite reported as outbreak cases rise
item.description: The first two cyclosporiasis-related deaths were reported in Michigan. This comes as Sen. Richard Blumenthal, a Democrat from Connecticut, calls for an investigation into Taylor Farms' connections to the Trump administration. CBS News' Dr. Céline Gounder weighs in.

item.title: Can you qualify for debt forgiveness after a divorce?
item.description: A divorce can have a big impact on your finances — and your debt. Here's what to know before seeking forgiveness.

item.title: Trump says he's "really disappointed" with Pirro amid Reflecting Pool case
item.description: President Trump met in the Oval Office on Monday with U.S. attorney Jeanine Pirro after Pirro admitted poor installation caused the damage to the D.C. Reflecting Pool, not vandalism. Mr. Trump publicly slammed Pirro for her comments. Nicole Sganga has more.

item.title: Ariana Grande speaks out at concert about her plans to step back following tour
item.description: One day after announcing she'll step back from the spotlight after her tour ends, Ariana Grande spoke directly to fans at Monday night's show in Chicago. The singer said the decision was her own and "was made from a thoughtful and empowered place."

item.title: Drone hits crowded Russian beach, killing 7 people
item.description: A drone hit a packed beach in southern Russia on Monday on the Black Sea coast. Russian officials say seven people were killed and dozens were injured. Holly Williams reports.

item.title: Jordan Roth on going from behind the scenes on Broadway to in front of the camera
item.description: Tony Award-winning producer Jordan Roth talks about starring in the "The Shards" and describes what it was like to go from behind the scenes on Broadway to making his major on-screen acting debut.

item.title: Exclusive discounts from CBS Mornings Deals
item.description: On this edition of CBS Mornings Deals, we show you items that will help improve your everyday lifestyle. Visit cbsdeals.com to take advantage of these exclusive deals today. CBS earns commissions on purchases made through cbsdeals.com.

item.title: Splitting expenses? Here's the best way to talk about money with your friends
item.description: A new report from Zelle found 76% of Gen Z have fronted money for a group expense and were never fully repaid. Elaine Swann, an etiquette expert, shares how to have money conversations with friends if you're splitting expenses.

item.title: Simple ways to protect your skin during the summer
item.description: Dr. Elizabeth Hale, a clinical associate professor of dermatology at NYU Grossman School of Medicine, speaks to "CBS Mornings" about summer skincare routines, if there are any products to avoid and ways to prevent sunburn.

item.title: Boy saved in rip current rescue speaks out: "I thought I was going to ... die"
item.description: Last month, a 16-year-old lifeguard rescued 10-year-old Nathaniel Rai, who was struggling in a rip current off Santa Cruz, California. Rai and his father spoke to "CBS Mornings" about how the terrifying situation unfolded and their gratitude for the teen lifeguard who stepped in to help.

item.title: 2 deaths reported in cyclosporiasis outbreak, health officials say
item.description: The Michigan Department of Health confirms two people have died after contracting cyclosporiasis. The department said both individuals "had significant underlying health conditions that may have been impacted by cyclosporiasis and dehydration." Carter Evans reports.

item.title: How two versions of the Democratic Party are on display in Michigan's Senate primary
item.description: Moderate Rep. Haley Stevens and progressive Abdul El-Sayed are facing off in a race that is highlighting party divisions. CBS News' Ed O'Keefe has the latest on the Michigan Senate primary.

item.title: "Peanut butter" pay raises are out, as employers shift to merit hikes
item.description: Here's what employees can expect for a raise in 2027 as companies move away from broad-based pay increases.

item.title: Arson suspect in Spokane-area wildfire had prior manslaughter conviction
item.description: More than 700 buildings in the Spokane area have been destroyed and 400 more haven't been assessed, officials said as three fires burned in the area and an arrest was made in connection with one of them.

item.title: Senate candidate Haley Stevens stands firm on backing U.S. military aid to Israel
item.description: Michigan Rep. Haley Stevens, one of two Democrats in the primary for her party's Senate nomination, stands firm on backing U.S. military aid to Israel and claims opponent Abdul El-Sayed doesn't recognize Israel's right to exist.

item.title: 3 lions die at zoo as Japan bakes in "cruelly hot" summer
item.description: Ten of the 16 lions in Tama Zoological Park have suffered symptoms such as "loss of appetite and decreased activity" since mid-July, and three lionesses died, the zoo said.

item.title: Trump says Jeanine Pirro "choked" in dropping Reflecting Pool cases
item.description: "She folded like an umbrella," President Trump said of Jeanine Pirro, U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia.

item.title: Senate candidate El-Sayed questions assumption Michigan voters are moderates
item.description: Populist Abdul El-Sayed and Rep. Haley Stevens top the Democratic field going into Tuesday's Senate primary. Former Rep. Mike Rogers is running unopposed for the GOP nomination.

item.title: Dr. Anthony Fauci on pandemics, partisan critics, and "the psyche of the country"
item.description: Millions today owe their lives to the work of the man who devoted his career to public health, but in recent years Dr. Anthony Fauci has been targeted by a partisan, anti-science spectrum of opponents.
